Broker/backend settings are read from environment variables so the
application can run against a local Redis or a managed service, and
tests can switch to an eager/in-memory mode.

)

)

}

).lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")

result_serializer = "json"
accept_content = ["json"]
timezone = "UTC"

Implemented the async email notification system:

- **`celery_config.py`** — broker URL (`redis://localhost:6379/0`), result backend (`redis://localhost:6379/1`), task routes (`celery_app.send_notification_email` → `email` queue), plus `CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER` support for tests. All env-overridable.

- **`app.py`** — `PUT /tasks/{id}` dispatches `send_notification_email.delay(...)` when status transitions to `completed` (uses the owner's email, defaults to `username@example.com`, wrapped in try/except so the response is never blocked). Added `email` column migration to the users table.
- **`tests/test_notifications.py`** — 6 tests covering dispatch on completion, no dispatch for other statuses / already-completed, title used, default email, and the task's mock logging.
